features.description: Triage model: a single pure, total classifier that assigns every operator item exactly one operator_bucket, derived (never producer-asserted) from resolution_class + automatable + audience + reconciled gate-state + safety_class (consumed from the repair projection, not moved onto the ActionItem envelope). Buckets: needs_auth, needs_decision, agent_runnable, auto_safe, quiet, uncertain. uncertain is the fail-closed default for missing/stale inputs and is surfaced, never silently hidden. The model emits a canonical serialization plus a data_quality envelope (counts per bucket, count uncertain, staleness/source provenance). A pinned fixture of that serialization is the parity anchor so any consumer reads identical model output — model parity is asserted HERE, not inside a renderer.
steps: Define the operator_bucket closed enum + a pure classify(item, gate_state, plan_status) returning exactly one bucket; uncertain fail-closed
Keep the four axes distinct (resolution_class / automatable / safety_class / operator_bucket); document auto_safe as the reversible-derived-state subset of automatable
Emit a canonical serialization + a data_quality envelope (per-bucket counts, uncertain count, per-item provenance/staleness reasons)
Pin the serialization as a fixture (the parity anchor every consumer reads)
Test on the real 313-item fleet fixture: every item gets exactly one bucket; uncertain items carry a data-quality reason; classifier is pure and deterministic
features.acceptance: A pure, total operator-bucket classifier, a canonical serialization, and a data_quality envelope exist as the single source of truth. Verified by unit tests over a real fleet fixture proving totality (every item exactly one bucket), the uncertain fail-closed default with a recorded reason, determinism, the four axes staying distinct (auto_safe a strict subset of automatable), and a pinned-serialization parity fixture any consumer can read. No producer asserts operator_bucket; no renderer is referenced.

features.description: Deduplicate operator items by stable dedupe_key before bucketing, so the same gate/finding stops appearing 6-8 times. Collapse preserves the richest representative (most evidence, freshest) and records the collapsed count.
steps: Group items by dedupe_key; collapse to one representative + a duplicate_count
Choose the representative deterministically (freshest updated_at, then most evidence)
Test on real data: the duplicated approval items collapse to one-per-unique-plan-gate
features.acceptance: Items sharing a dedupe_key collapse to a single representative carrying a duplicate_count, deterministically. Verified by a test on the real fleet fixture showing the approval items (currently 6-8x per gate) collapse to one per unique plan/gate.

features.description: Reconcile gate items against plan status so closed/abandoned plans stop surfacing as live approvals. A gate whose plan status is completed or abandoned, or whose features all pass, reconciles to cleared and drops out of needs_decision; genuinely-live gates remain. Reconciliation reasons feed the data_quality envelope (a reconciled-stale gate is recorded, not silently dropped).
steps: Define the stale-gate predicate: plan status in {completed, abandoned} OR all features pass
Reconcile each gate item: stale -> cleared (out of needs_decision), recorded with a reason
Test on real data: known-closed plans' gates no longer surface as needs_decision; an active plan's live gate still does
features.acceptance: Gate items are reconciled against plan status; stale gates (closed/abandoned plan, or all features pass) leave needs_decision with a recorded reconciliation reason, while live gates remain. Verified by a test asserting known-closed plans drop out of needs_decision and an active plan's live gate persists.

features.description: dontpanic operator brief (--json|--text): the agent-facing render. Reads the F001 canonical serialization and emits the per-bucket lists, each item carrying its exact command, dedupe_key, operator_bucket, depends_on, and an evidence reference; a top-level allow-list (agent_runnable + auto_safe, with commands) vs escalate-list (needs_auth + needs_decision); and the data_quality block. Carries an explicit honesty contract (like the agent-manifest safety_rules): narrate uncertain, never fabricate a clean bucket, never run human-gated items. Named operator brief to avoid colliding with the existing agent brief setup surface. This is a command-line surface only.
steps: Add the operator-brief command reading the F001 canonical serialization
Emit --json: buckets + per-item command/deps/evidence + allow-list/escalate-list + data_quality
Emit --text: a tight agent/human-readable digest of the same
Embed the honesty contract; surface uncertain + staleness as first-class
Journey tests A1/A2/A3/A4 on real state: an agent derives a run-plan + escalation list; the escalate-list equals needs_auth+needs_decision; uncertainty is reported, not hidden
features.acceptance: operator brief --json and --text render the F001 model with an allow-list vs escalate-list, the data_quality block, and an embedded honesty contract. Verified by journey tests on real state: an agent boots and derives a run-plan + precise escalation list (A1), the safe-to-run set excludes everything human-gated (A2), the output suffices to report back what an agent ran (A3), and incomplete classification surfaces as uncertain, never fabricated (A4). Command-line surface only.

features.description: Safe-tier application engine (command-line only): dontpanic triage apply --safe is a command the human or an agent runs in their terminal. It applies ONLY auto_safe (reversible derived-state) items. Dry-run is the default (prints what would run, why each is safe, expected file changes); --confirm runs them; every run writes a logged, reversible evidence record (what ran, why safe, what changed, what confirmed it). Hard refusals: never credentials (needs_auth), never approvals (needs_decision), never project mutations. Off by default; a config flag may later enable unattended apply for pure cache/state projection only. Needed in v0 because the agent run-plan (A2) and the auto_safe handoff require a real command to exist.
steps: Implement triage apply --safe over the auto_safe bucket only; dry-run default
On --confirm: run, then write an evidence record (ran/why-safe/changed/confirmed); reversible
Refuse needs_auth / needs_decision / project-mutating items with a clear reason
Tests: dry-run mutates nothing; --confirm applies only auto_safe + logs evidence; refusals hold
features.acceptance: triage apply --safe (command-line) applies only the auto_safe bucket, dry-run by default, with a logged reversible evidence record on --confirm, and hard refuses credentials/approvals/project mutations. Verified by tests proving dry-run is side-effect-free, --confirm applies only auto_safe items and writes evidence, and a needs_auth/needs_decision/mutation item is refused. Disabled by default; runnable by a human or agent in a terminal.

features.description: Operator console — default view (workbench left pane + top bar). The human-facing console renders the F001 model as a calm default screen supporting observer mode (glance while working elsewhere) and the entry to operator mode. One honest status line (H5); the needs-you list of ALL unique live needs_auth + needs_decision items (deduped + gate-reconciled, each one sentence, Uncertain riding WITH them); and a blocked-explainer (the block, the one move, the consequence, H4). Non-human buckets collapse behind a single 'handled' count whose click FILTERS the same left queue (never opens a separate grid). One accent colour for needs-you; muted otherwise; no raw JSON; no repeated banners. The human-item count is whatever is genuinely live — NOT capped. NAMED DEPENDENCY: build writes fleet state to the operator-home dashboard dir while serve reads the repo dashboard state dir — this feature resolves or explicitly defers that serve-path so real fleet data renders.
steps: Render the default view from the F001 model: status line + the full live needs-you list (Uncertain included) + blocked-explainer; collapse handled to counts that filter the same queue
Apply the calm rules: one accent, two type sizes, no raw JSON, no repeated banners
Resolve or defer the fleet-state serve-path so real fleet data renders (name it in decisions)

Correctness journey test H1 on real fleet state: the default view shows ALL unique live needs_auth+needs_decision (deduped+gate-reconciled), non-human buckets collapsed, zero raw JSON, one status line
Separate fixture assertion: the real 313-item fleet collapses to its expected unique-human count (derived from the data, not a hard cap)
features.acceptance: The default console view renders the F001 model as a calm queue: one health line, the FULL set of unique live needs_auth+needs_decision items (Uncertain included, deduped+gate-reconciled), a blocked-explainer, handled work collapsed to filtering counts. Verified by (1) a correctness journey test (H1/H4/H5) on real fleet state asserting the view shows exactly the unique live human items, non-human collapsed, zero raw JSON, one status line — NO hard count cap; and (2) a separate fixture assertion that the real 313-item inventory collapses to its expected unique-human count. The fleet-state serve-path dependency is resolved or explicitly deferred in decisions. Browser/GUI surface only.

features.description: Operator console — inspect surfaces (workbench right pane + activity strip). The decision drawer (select a gate -> its audit findings, diff summary, plan acceptance, signoff, enough to decide from evidence in place, H3); the what-was-handled log rendered as the bottom activity strip (reverse-chron, plain language: what the agent/auto ran, why safe, what changed, evidence ref, H2) carrying the '313 -> N unique -> M need you' pipeline line; and the why-hidden inspector (expand a handled count into the same queue, each item tagged with its bucket AND the reason it is there — deduped / stale-reconciled / info / agent-runnable, H6). The activity strip and the what-was-handled log are ONE evidence source rendered as ambient chrome. Browser/GUI surface only; reads evidence, executes nothing.
steps: Right pane: render a gate's evidence (findings, diff, acceptance, signoff) for an in-place decision
Activity strip: render the one evidence source (agent/auto actions + the pipeline line) as an ambient reverse-chron log
Why-hidden: expand a handled count into the same queue with per-item bucket + reason
Journey tests H2/H3/H6 on real state: a human can decide one gate from its evidence; see what was handled + verify; see why each hidden item was hidden
features.acceptance: The console provides a right-pane decision drawer, a bottom activity strip (= the one what-was-handled evidence source, carrying the pipeline line), and a why-hidden inspector over the F001 model. Verified by journey tests on real state: a human decides a gate from its surfaced evidence without reading source (H3), audits what the agent/auto ran and confirms it (H2), and sees why each hidden item was suppressed with its bucket + reason (H6). Reads evidence only; no execution.

features.description: Operator console — handoff actions (workbench center pane + mode switch), V0 = COPY / OPEN / MARK-RUN / REFRESH ONLY. The console NEVER originates a mutation; it expresses intent and hands the exact command to the human or a chosen agent to execute in a terminal/Cursor/Claude/Codex/Grok. Per bucket: needs_decision exposes approve/request-changes/reject INTENT, then copy the exact command (e.g. the dontpanic approve command for that gate) or open-terminal — no browser-originated approval. auto_safe exposes copy of the dry-run command and the --confirm command (the F005 engine), or open-terminal — no browser-originated apply. agent_runnable exposes copy-command, copy-run-plan, and open-in-terminal/agent (v0 'send to agent' = copy-run-plan / open-terminal, NOT live dispatch to a running agent). mark-run-externally + attach-evidence is itself a COMMAND HANDOFF (a generated command the human/agent runs to record evidence), not a GUI-originated file write. refresh re-reads the F001 model after external action. Observer mode hides the intent/handoff controls; Operator mode shows them and is visually unmistakable; either way nothing executes from the browser. Browser-originated governed mutation (real approve/apply from the console) is explicitly OUT — deferred to plan 2026-06-06-002 (D018).
steps: Define the per-bucket handoff affordance model and render it on each center-pane card
needs_decision: approve/request-changes/reject intent -> copy the exact command / open-terminal (no browser mutation)
auto_safe: copy the dry-run + --confirm commands / open-terminal (no browser apply)
agent_runnable: copy-command / copy-run-plan / open-in-terminal-or-agent (copy/open, not live dispatch)
mark-run-externally: generate the evidence-recording command to hand off; refresh re-reads the F001 model
Observer/Operator mode toggle (loud); Journey tests H7 + A5 on real state: every path is copy/open/handoff and the console executes nothing
features.acceptance: The console center pane exposes per-bucket COPY/OPEN/MARK-RUN/REFRESH handoff: needs_decision -> approve/request-changes/reject intent then copy-command/open-terminal; auto_safe -> copy dry-run + --confirm commands / open-terminal; agent_runnable -> copy-command/copy-run-plan/open-in-terminal-or-agent; mark-run-externally -> a generated evidence-recording command; refresh -> re-read the F001 model. Verified by journey tests H7 + A5 on real state proving the console ORIGINATES NO mutation (every action is copy/open/handoff), Observer mode hides the controls and Operator mode shows them (loud), and refresh re-reads the model after an external agent/terminal acted. Browser-originated governed mutation is out of scope (deferred to 2026-06-06-002).
